title: Randomized Experiment Design
interviewAnswer: A trustworthy experiment starts with a unit of randomization, eligibility criteria, treatment assignment, primary metric, guardrails and a pre-specified analysis plan. Randomization protects causal interpretation when implementation is correct.
keyPoints: Define exposure and sample ratio checks.
Primary metrics and guardrails should be decided before reading results.
why: Randomized Experiment Design appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: A trustworthy experiment starts with a unit of randomization, eligibility criteria, treatment assignment, primary metric, guardrails and a pre-specified analysis plan. Randomization protects causal interpretation when implementation is correct. Define exposure and sample ratio checks. Primary metrics and guardrails should be decided before reading results. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Randomize users to a new recommendation algorithm while monitoring conversion plus latency and complaint-rate guardrails.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Randomized Experiment Design make?
How would you validate or debug Randomized Experiment Design in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
